name: G-ParSNIP: frozen ZTF-trained ParSNIP decoder (wave-2 fold 0) as a forward-model grader
roles_all_from_code: encoder in the FM arm tool only (parsnip_run.py -> ParsnipModel.predict_sncosmo); the grader never encodes
code_pin: grader_private/forward_models.py sha256 302586fd569997382bd9d46a564722c0d91410a79cad6ebef556a665d677d36f; kboone/parsnip@dcea62f copy in data_cache/grader_pinned/parsnip_code (per-file pins PARSNIP_CODE_PINS): sncosmo.py ParsnipSncosmoSource L12-69, parsnip.py predict_sncosmo L1667-1717, decode_spectra L856-893
quantity_returned: ParsnipSncosmoSource._flux: decode_spectra(encoding=(s1,s2,s3), phase x SIDEREAL_SCALE, color, amplitude) -> rest-frame spectra on the model wavelength grid, linearly interpolated, wrapped in sncosmo.Model with z, t0 and F99 MW dust at item mwebv; bandflux in ztfg/ztfr at ZP 25 AB. Defined over phase -250..+250 d and 1000-11000 A.
defining_paper: Boone 2021, AJ 162, 275, arXiv:2109.13999 (read in full by wave-1 agent 4). Weights: wave-2 agent 4 per-fold training, compositions_FROZEN.md section 7.
accuracy_against_scored_measurement: Synthetic only: truth on CTRL-PARSNIP (an item generated by the same decoder) S = 0.313, wrong set (t0+15, color+0.5) S = 238.6. This tests the arithmetic of the path, not whether the decoder can predict real light curves at held-out phases, which is UNDEMONSTRATED and at risk (see disagreements).
what_it_is_not: Not trained at the scored phases: every training light curve was truncated at E1 or E3 (<= night n0+3 after first detection, features.py truncate), so predictions 10-60 d after first detection are extrapolation of the decoder. Not a released checkpoint. Not a redshift estimator in this configuration (photo-z prior neutralised). Not float64: parameters and phases are cast to float32 in _flux.
conventions: sncosmo parameter names z, t0, amplitude, color, s1, s2, s3; amplitude in sncosmo units (predict_sncosmo applies parsnip_scale x 10^(-0.4 x 45))
MW dust F99 forward in grader; ParSNIP preprocessing corrects input with FM07
shipped plasticc/ps1 checkpoints removed from both copies

served_checkpoint.identifier: wave-2 parsnip_fold0.pt (ztfg, ztfr; predict_redshift True; lr 1e-4; 60 epochs; 2724 training units)

disagreements.paper: Boone 2021 trains on full light curves
disagreements.code: wave-2 fold models were trained only on light curves truncated at E1/E3 (features.py truncate), so the decoder has no training support 10-60 d after first detection

disagreements.paper: code instruments.py applies FM07 R_V=3.1 correction to ZTF inputs

disagreements.code: _flux casts parameters and phase to torch.FloatTensor (float32); float perturbations below ~1e-7 relative are invisible, which is why the v1 must-not-fire control passed for ParSNIP alone

disagreements.paper: Sec 6.8: the decoder can predict any band
disagreements.code: ParsnipSncosmoSource integrates spectra through sncosmo ztfg/ztfr; the training-time band weights are not used by the grader path

construct_validity_I4.question: Does the held-out residual measure what the program scores?
construct_validity_I4.scored_quantity: generate / inverse problem: the predictive adequacy of a submitted forward model (family + parameters) for photometry the arm never saw, i.e. the oracle's verdict on whether the generated object meets the constraint 'reproduces the later light curve' (shape.md A3 row for generate).
construct_validity_I4.ruling: PASS for predictive fit on held-out ZTF g/r difference photometry in (t_first+10, t_first+60] d. FAIL as a measure of physical truth (true class, true redshift, true explosion physics): no term in S depends on whether the parameters are physically correct, only on whether the forward model reproduces the later fluxes. Any program claim must be worded as predictive fit, never as correct physical inference.
weaknesses: Degeneracy: physically wrong parameters (wrong z with compensating x0/x1/c, or a flexible Bazin/Villar curve) can predict the held-out fluxes as well as correct ones; S cannot separate them.

Family asymmetry in model range: SALT3 returns 0 flux outside rest-frame -20..+50 d, ParSNIP is defined over +-250 d, parametric curves everywhere; late held-out points therefore penalise SALT3 by construction, a property of the family and not of the arm.
The 5% error floor down-weights high-S/N points and sets the scale at which systematic model error is forgiven; a different floor re-orders submissions near the floor.
Equal band weighting: a band with 5 points counts as much as one with 20.
Held-out residuals within a band are correlated (host subtraction residuals, calibration offsets per field/night), so N_b overstates independent information.
Horizon choice: the +60 d window mixes peak and early decline; a different horizon changes which family is favoured (e.g. Villar plateau vs SALT3 cut-off).
model covariance (SALT3 modelcov) is excluded from S, so SALT3's own stated model uncertainty is not credited.
Rejected-rival reasons are recorded but not scored; the written-rejection branch has no grader.
Near-zero or negative fluxes (pre-explosion or late) are scored like any other point; a baseline B term in parametric families can absorb them, SN families cannot.
Separation is procedural (brief constraint 3): if an arm reads grader_private/, the residual measures memorised data, not prediction.
construct_validity_I4.family_specific: UNDEMONSTRATED for real items beyond the training window; the grader evaluates the decoder faithfully, but a poor ParSNIP score cannot be attributed to the arm rather than to the truncated training set.

certification_I5: Known-input PASS and negative control PASS on a decoder-generated item; must-not-fire PASS at v1 and v2. Status: CERTIFIED for the arithmetic path on synthetic input; I4 on real data UNDEMONSTRATED.
